narrative.overview:
This is the record an engineer keeps while building: ruled entries, real measurements, annotations in the margin where something needs saying. It is not a gallery and not a brochure. The reader is usually skimming — a recruiter with a minute, a faculty member reading harder — so the page's job is to let evidence be found fast and then reward someone who slows down.

The system is light by decision rather than by convention. Its use scene is a phone in an office and a laptop at a desk, both under room light, both reading rather than monitoring; a dark ground would have served neither. Structure comes from rules and tonal bands rather than from boxes, because the content is a long ranked list of real work and card grids flatten ranking into sameness. Purdue's old gold is the one non-neutral material, and it only ever marks.

The notebook is literal in three places and nowhere else: graph-paper stock that fades as you scroll into long reading, line figures sketched in the margins that are worked-out problems rather than decoration, and a gold-topped annotation block carrying contribution scope. What the system does not take from the notebook is untidiness — nothing is skewed, torn, taped, or set in a handwriting face.
keyCharacteristics: Light ground, near-black ink, cool neutral rules; no dark mode
Ruled lists as the primary structure; cards only as selectors
One spacing rhythm across every surface, more space above a heading than below
Gold as material, never as type
Monospace strictly for real data — years, languages, ranks, counts
Graph-paper stock beneath everything, masked away before it can disturb reading
Marginal line figures drawn from Kevin's own problems, never stock engineering art
Every media-bearing surface is designed to be complete with no media present
Motion never hides content, on any surface, for any duration

rules.name: The Gold-Is-Material Rule
rules.body: Old Gold is a rule, a border, or a highlight — never a letterform. At the sizes this system sets type, #cfb991 cannot hold 4.5:1 against paper, so if gold text is wanted the answer is Deep Gold or a different idea.

rules.name: The Wayfinding-Only Rule
rules.body: A division hue may tint a rule, a marker, a border, or a small label. It may not fill a region, a card, or a section background.

rules.name: The Blue-Means-Clickable Rule
rules.body: Record Blue appears on interactive text and nothing else. No decorative use, ever.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Measured Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where a real value is reported. It is never a texture for 'technical'. If a mono label has no value behind it, it should be body text.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No kicker or eyebrow line above a heading. Headings carry their own weight.

rules.name: The One-Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Every section break uses --section-y. A surface that needs to feel tighter or looser adjusts its internal padding, not the section rhythm.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat until something happens to them. The reel stage is the single exception, because it is a display.

rules.name: The Never-Hide-Content Rule
rules.body: No animation may start from opacity: 0, and no content may depend on script or scroll to become readable. The settle animation floors at 0.55 opacity, is applied only by JavaScript, is never applied to the first section on screen, and does nothing under prefers-reduced-motion.

dos: Do use the ruled list for any collection of work. It ranks; a grid does not.
Do state contribution scope on anything collaborative, in the annotation block.
Do design every media slot to look finished with nothing in it.
Do keep monospace tied to a real reported value.
Do put separation in a tonal band or a hairline before reaching for a shadow.
Do route every internal link through url() in src/lib/site.ts.
Do keep all four division destinations visible on mobile.
Do draw any new marginal figure from something Kevin actually built, at 1px on the 200-unit grid, and place it only where the paper is genuinely empty.
donts: Don't set type in Old Gold (#cfb991); it cannot hold contrast. Use Deep Gold.
Don't fill a region with a division hue.
Don't add a dark mode. Light is a decision about the reading scene.
Don't introduce a card grid as page structure, or nest cards.
Don't add an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't use a zero-blur or zero-offset shadow; every shadow has both.
Don't write the header height as a literal anywhere — use --header-h.
Don't let the demo reel depend on JavaScript for its links to work.
Don't animate anything from opacity: 0, or let scroll position decide whether content is legible.
Don't add stock engineering decoration — gears, circuit traces, blueprints.
Don't place a marginal figure over a column that carries text.
Don't invent a competitive result, date, role, or metric.
